summary.text: A 60-year-old male from a low socioeconomic background presented with left flank pain and weight loss. Because urolithiasis was clinically suspected he was referred for imaging. There was no flank tenderness on examination, but a few enlarged cervical and inguinal lymph nodes were found.

Urine analysis showed albuminuria 2+, numerous leucocytes and a negative nitrite test; microscopy found 227 RBCs, 314 WBCs and 239 bacteria per high power field, yet bacterial culture showed no growth, indicating sterile pyuria. Renal tuberculosis was considered, with chronic pyelonephritis as the differential diagnosis.

Plain CT showed disproportionately dilated upper pole calyces, urothelial thickening with pelvic narrowing, lower pole papillary calcifications, fat stranding and lymphadenopathy. CT urogram showed calyceal filling defects, papillary cavities, infundibular-pelvic stenosis and signs of papillary necrosis. Static MR urogram showed the same calyceal findings without contrast, plus a dilated ureter narrowing at its insertion suggesting a stricture.

Urine culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The patient was started on antitubercular chemotherapy and put on follow-up with a plan to perform ureteric stenting. Cystoscopy confirmed a thickened and narrowed left ureteric opening characteristic of tuberculosis. No outcome after treatment is reported.

ambiguities.issue: Figure 3 caption places the CT blunt-tipped calyces in the right lower pole, while Figure 4 (MR) is of the left kidney and its ring sign corresponds to Figure 3b, and cystoscopy involves the left ureteric opening.
